haiku-low.q1: It replies 202 with the rejected events listed, only after the accepted events are appended to the log and every in-sync replica confirms.
haiku-low.q2: The client resends the same batch with the same event_ids, waiting 1 second before the first retry, doubling up to a 5-minute cap.
haiku-low.q3: The first-received copy wins: the live dedup store keeps the first copy it accepts, and replay keeps the earliest received_at.
haiku-low.q4: It belongs to Tuesday's partition, since its day is set by received_at, and is rebuilt by replay of Tuesday.
haiku-low.q5: A key-value store keyed by event_id; each entry holds received_at, partition day and micro-batch ID. Store expiry removes keys 8 days after they are set.
haiku-low.q6: The live consumer pauses, writing nothing unchecked; lag grows, and the 14-day log retention covers the pause. Collector behavior: NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q7: Each micro-batch commits as one transaction keyed by consumer group and offset range, so a retry cannot double-insert; restart resumes from the last committed offset.
haiku-low.q8: Input: raw archive copies in object storage, partitions D-7 through D. Rebuilt rows go to a tagged staging table, then swap into events_clean.
haiku-low.q9: Replay keeps each event_id's earliest-received copy, read from raw partitions D-7 through D; it keeps only winners received on D.
haiku-low.q10: Failed checks drop the staging table, leaving the live partition unchanged; the swap is one transaction, so no mixed state. Recovery for other failures: NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q11: Closed days D, once 02:00 UTC on D+1 has passed, and before D+80; one replay per day at a time.
haiku-low.q12: NOT DECIDED: product must choose drop or keep-with-flag; the plan chooses neither, placed between enrichment and load.

sonnet.q1: It replies 202 with a list of rejected events (position in batch plus reason); the other events are accepted. It may reply only after appending the accepted events to the log and every in-sync replica has confirmed. If the append fails for any part, it replies 503 for the whole batch (400 if the body is unparseable or over 100 events).
sonnet.q2: It resends the same batch with the same event_ids, backing off 1 second first, doubling each time, capped at 5 minutes. The mobile SDK keeps unacknowledged events on the device up to 7 days. Rejected events are never resent.
sonnet.q3: Live: the first copy the dedup store accepts (later copy is dropped from the clean path) provided it arrives while the key exists (8-day expiry). After replay of a closed day: the copy with the earliest received_at wins (ties: lower node ID, then lower batch sequence), and replay is authoritative.
sonnet.q4: Tuesday's partition (UTC day of received_at, 00:10 UTC Tuesday). The client timestamp does not decide the partition or replay. It is replayed with Tuesday's replay (day D = Tuesday).
sonnet.q5: In the dedup store, a key-value store with one key per event_id. Each value holds received_at, the partition day and the ID of the micro-batch that claims the event. Keys expire 8 days after being set; later copies do not reset the expiry.
sonnet.q6: The live consumer pauses and writes no unchecked rows. Lag grows, and the clients' events are still accepted by the collector and stored in the log (kept 14 days) and archived. Live dedup is broken for the open day if keys are lost; the recovery procedure is still to be written.
sonnet.q7: Nothing is lost because the consumer re-reads the log from its last committed offset. No double-counting because the micro-batch load commits as one transaction with an idempotency key built from consumer group and offset range, so a retry does not insert the same rows twice. Also, on re-run, dedup keys with the same batch ID mean the event is kept rather than dropped as a duplicate.
sonnet.q8: It reads only the raw archive in object storage (partitions D-7 through D, duplicates included). Rebuilt rows are written to a staging table tagged with the replay run ID; events_clean is not changed until the swap.
sonnet.q9: It uses a stateless rule. It reads all raw copies for D-7 through D, and for each event_id keeps the earliest received_at copy (ties: lower collector node ID, then lower batch sequence). It keeps only winners whose winning copy was received on D. Events with a first copy on an earlier day (within D-7) have an earlier winner and so are not in D.
sonnet.q10: The live partition is unchanged, because replay writes only to a staging table and a failed validation check drops the staging table. The swap is one warehouse transaction, so readers see the old or new partition, never a mix. NOT STATED: an explicit operator recovery procedure for a crash partway (beyond the lock/run being recorded and the live partition remaining intact; presumably the operator reruns, but this is not stated).
sonnet.q11: A closed day D, at or after 02:00 UTC on D+1, and before D+80 (refused from D+80 onward). Only one replay per day at a time. Impossible after about D+83 because raw data expires.
sonnet.q12: Not decided. Product has not decided whether to drop it or keep it with a flag. The plan chooses neither; the decision goes after enrichment and before the load. Replay applies whatever decision is in force.
